jobs.occupation: Research Assistant/Doctoral Student (f/m/d) - Chair of Behavioral Accounting (Research-Manager/in)
jobs.employer_name: WHU – Otto Beisheim School of Management-1
jobs.description: General informationThe new Chair of Behavioral Accounting ( Prof. Dr. Victor van Pel t) at WHU – Otto Beisheim School of Management in Vallendar is dedicated to the empirical and experimental analysis of decision-making behavior in accounting settings. The focus is on behavioral accounting, controlled, online, and field experiments, and contemporary trends like the use of artificial intelligence. Our research examines how controls, performance feedback, and reporting choices shape the judgments and decisions of managers, employees, investors, and other firm stakeholders. WHU has an international orientation, offers an excellent research environment, and has a vibrant doctoral programme. Moreover, our chair is part of the Finance and Accounting Group, which organizes frequent reading groups and research seminars that further strengthen your doctoral training. This position is particularly suited for people (f/m/d) interested in behavioral research, with a focus on accounting questions, and a career in academia.Your mission Research• Conducting independent research in the field of behavioral accounting, in particular on experimental issues in reporting, controls, performance feedback, and the use of artificial intelligence in accounting.• The aim is to present research results at international conferences and publish them in leading journals.Teaching• Collaboration in the implementation and further development of courses in the field of financial and management accounting (e.g. preparation of materials, supervision of students, data analysis or support with experiments).• Opportunity to gradually take on your own teaching responsibilities and further develop your teaching skills as part of your doctoral programme.Doctoral programme• Active participation in WHU’s structured doctoral programme, which includes methodological and theoretical courses, research seminars, and presentations in the doctoral colloquium.• Use of the international research environment for professional and personal development, including access to laboratory and online recruitment resources and support for conference travel.Your profileAcademic background• Above-average master’s degree in accounting, economics, finance or a related area.• Ideally, your master’s thesis was written in a subject area related to behavioral or experimental research.• We particularly value if you’ve finished a preparation track, like a research master or another specialized graduate research program.Technical and methodological skills• Strong mathematical programming, analytical, and critical thinking skills.• Experience with experimental design, statistical inference, and academic research and writing practices.• Proficiency in at least one of the following statistical programming languages: R, Stata, or Python.• Experience with oTree for conducting experiments is a big plus.Research interests• Strong interest in experimental behavioral research, particularly in the areas of accounting.• Interest in topics such as misreporting, performance measurement and feedback, controls, incentives, and contemporary issues like sustainability and the use of AI is particularly welcome.Personal requirements• A passion for learning and scientific research in an international environment.• Excellent written and spoken English proficiency (German proficiency is not required).What we offer Academic EnvironmentWHU has more than 60 faculty members in the fields of management, finance and accounting, economics, entrepreneurship and innovation, marketing and sales, and supply chain management. Research at WHU aims to adhere to three principles: quality, internationality, and practical relevance.WHU is an equal opportunity employer and thus welcomes applications from individuals with diverse backgrounds. We believe in the benefits of diversity and therefore foster an international, inclusive, and inspiring working environment.ContactFor questions please contact:Professor Victor van Peltemail: Victor.vanPelt@whu.eduAbout usAs one of Germany’s top private business schools, WHU is consistently ranked among Europe’s finest. Since its inception in 1984, we have driven excellence and entrepreneurial thinking, producing innovative research that steers progress for all areas of society and industry. At both the Vallendar and Düsseldorf campuses, we empower leaders to become responsible changemakers, guided by integrity, diversity, and strengthened by a deep sense of togetherness.

jobs.occupation: Lecturer Akademische Rätin/Akademischer Rat auf Zeit (salary level A 13 LBesO) (Biologe/Biologin)
jobs.description: Creating knowledge. Making a difference. Shaping the future. This is what the University of Münster stands for as one of the strongest research-oriented universities in Germany and one of the largest employers in the region. Every day, over 7,000 employees devote themselves to cutting-edge research and excellent teaching. We share more than a workplace. We share the desire to make a real impact – regionally and internationally. Our day-to-day work is distinguished by diversity, openness and space to pursue one’s ideas. Become a part of our team – in academia, a technical or manual trade, or administration.The Molecular Evolution and Sociobiology Group (AG Gadau) at the Institute for Evolution and Biodiversity (IEB) at the University of Münster, Germany, is seeking to fill the position of aLecturerAkademische Rätin/Akademischer Rat auf Zeit(salary level A 13 LBesO)commencing on 01 January 2027. We are offering a three-year, fixed-term position (100%) with the option to extend by an additional three years. The prospective candidate is required to teach four hours per week during the semester (4 SWS).Your tasks:- Developing an independent, internationally visible and competitive research program in Evolutionary Biology, Molecular Evolution or Chemical Ecology of Hymenoptera- Participating in teaching (4SWS/semester) of Bachelor/Master/PhD Students with the option of developing own teaching modules.- Participation in academic self-administrationOur expectations:- Having fun doing research and teaching in Evolutionary Biology.- A university degree and a PhD in Biology, or a related field is required.- Extensive experience in chemical ecology and either of the following two fields: molecular evolution or evolutionary ecology demonstrated by publications in peer reviewed articles is required.- Excellent command of English is required.- Postdoctoral research in evolutionary biology, evolutionary ecology, or chemical ecology is an advantage but not necessary.- Ideally you have willingness and motivation to work closely with students (BS, MS, PhD) in teaching and supervision.- Applications for Third-Party funding to build an own, sustainable and independent research program in Evolutionary Biology would be welcomed.- A high level of organizational and communication skills and readiness to collaborate on shared projects within the IEB/AG GadauAdvantages for you:- The AG Gadau and the Institute for Evolution and Biodiversity (https://www.uni-muenster.de/Evolution/ (https://www.uni-muenster.de/Evolution/) ) offer a wide range of opportunities for basic research and teaching in various areas of evolutionary biology, evolutionary ecology, bioinformatics, and biodiversity research.- The international and interdisciplinary teams at the IEB and within the AG Gadau foster a collaborative working environment and are actively involved in numerous national and international research. This creates ideal conditions for collaborations within these consortia as well as for independent research projects.-  Appreciation, commitment, openness and respect – values which are important to us.- Our broad range of diverse work-time models offers great flexibility – also when working from home.- If you have family members or young children in your care, our Family Service Office offers concrete support to help you balance your private and professional responsibilities.- As an educational institution, we are deeply committed to offering occupational training and continuing education opportunities tailored to your individual needs.- From A – Z, Aikido to Zumba, our sport and health programmes ensure a healthy work-life balance.The University of Münster strongly supports equal opportunity and diversity (https://www.uni-muenster.de/profil/en/diversity/policy/mission-statement.html) . We welcome all applicants regardless of sex, nationality, ethnic or social background, religion or worldview, disability, age, sexual orientation or gender identity. We are committed to creating family-friendly working conditions.We actively encourage applications by women. Women with equivalent qualifications and academic achievements will be preferentially considered unless these are outweighed by reasons which necessitate the selection of another candidate.If you have any questions, please contact Prof. Jürgen Gadau (gadauj@uni-muenster.de (gadauj@uni-muenster.de) ) or Dr. Lukas Schrader (lukas.schrader@uni-muenster.de (lukas.schrader@uni-muenster.de) ).Are you interested? Then we look forward to receiving your application (CV and 2-3-page description of your research plan) by 28-10-2026 exclusively via our online application portal.For sustainability reasons, we kindly ask you to refrain from submitting paper/printed documents.Universität MünsterProf. Dr. Jürgen GadauFaculty of BiologyInstitute for Evolution and BiodiversityHüfferstr. 148149 Münster https://www.uni-muenster.de/Evolution/index.shtml (https://www.uni-muenster.de/Evolution/index.shtml)Kennziffer: 3.1_2026_09_01

jobs.occupation: Doctoral researcher (m/f/d/x) in microbial systems biophysics (Biophysiker/in)
jobs.description: Founded in 1409, Leipzig University is one of Germany’s largest universities and a leader in research and medical training. With around 30,000 students and more than 5000 members of staff across 14 faculties, it is at the heart of the vibrant and outward-looking city of Leipzig. Leipzig University offers an innovative and international working environment as well as an exciting range of career opportunities in research, teaching, knowledge and technology transfer, infrastructure and administration.The Division of Systems Biophysics of Microbial Dynamics at the Peter Debye Institute for Soft Matter Physics at the Faculty of Physics and Earth System Sciences, seeks to fill the above position.About the position- Salary group 13 TV-L - Fixed-term position in accordance with the training plan, initially for 1 year; an extension of the fixed-term contract is planned- 50 % of a full-time position- As soon as possibleThe newly formed Division of Systems Biophysics of Microbial Dynamics (https://home.uni-leipzig.de/sysbiophys/) , led by Professor Katja Taute, is part of the Peter Debye Institute for Soft Matter Physics (https://www.physes.uni-leipzig.de/en/pdi) , which hosts a broad range of biophysics research. Active matter, including bacterial systems, is a growing key research area at the Institute. Our research group develops and uses biophysical methods, including high-throughput, 3D bacterial tracking and microfluidics, in combination with theory and simulations, to quantitatively analyse the spatio-temporal dynamics of bacteria at the level of individuals and populations. One research focus is the chemotactic navigation of bacteria in mechanically complex environments. In nature, swimming bacteria navigate relative to chemical stimuli in environments ranging from open waters to soil and the gut.The new doctoral researcher is to investigate how the gut bacterium E. coli navigates mechanically complex environments that mimic properties of its natural habitat. Properties of both the bacteria and the environment will be modulated in a controlled fashion to identify the underlying physical mechanisms and address the following questions:- What is the relationship between behavioural and material parameters that enable optimal navigation?- Is optimal intracellular information processing specific to the type of environment?- How do bacteria navigate mechanical gradients?The role- Independent, original, experimental scientific research on the above project- Additional scientific qualification (preparing a doctoral thesis)- Thorough documentation of research- Publication of research results, for example at conferences, workshops, or in scientific articles- Contributions to the Institute’s teaching responsibilitiesAbout you- An excellent scientific university degree (master of science or comparable) in (bio-)physics, (bio-)engineering or a related field- Very good command of at least one programming language (Matlab or Python preferred) and of quantitative scientific data analysis- A track record of academic excellence (e.g. very good grades in the course of study, research or study scholarships and prizes, scientific publications)- Written and spoken professional fluency in English (at least equivalent to level B2)- Excellent written communication skills, demonstrated through coherent, structured and precise writing- Experience with microscopy and scientific image processing would be an advantage- Interest in quantitative experimental interdisciplinary science- Collaborative mindset and teamwork skillsWhat we offer you- a varied role with a high degree of responsibility in the dynamic environment of a major university- a professional English-language work environment at the leading edge of interdisciplinary science- Collaboration in a friendly, supportive and motivated team- flexible working hours and mobile working to support work-life balance- Goal-oriented staff development throughout your working life, with opportunities for continuing professional development- a wide range of occupational health management services - Remuneration in line with the collective bargaining agreement of the federal states (TV-L), including an annual special payment and occupational pension scheme- excellent transport links and the option to purchase a discounted public transport ticket, such as the Deutschlandticket as a commuter pass- a wide range of food options in the refectories and cafés operated by Studentenwerk Leipzig.Leipzig University aims to increase the proportion of women in positions of responsibility and therefore expressly invites qualified women to apply. Severely disabled persons – or persons deemed legally equal to them under Book IX of the German Social Code – are encouraged to apply and will be given preference in the case of equal suitability. If you have any questions about accessibility or need assistance with this application process, please contact Leipzig University’s disability officers at: schwerbehindertenvertretung@uni-leipzig.de (https://mailto:schwerbehindertenvertretung@uni-leipzig.de) .Have we sparked your interest?Please submit your application in English addressed to Fakultät für Physik und Erdsystemwissenschaften, Herrn Dekan Professor Dr. Johannes Quaas by 1 November 2026 via our online application portal.Please include the following documents with your application:- A short letter of motivation (max. 1 page) in which you clearly explain why you would like to work on this project- A scientific CV (evidence of creative and independent scientific work is an advantage)- The names and contact information of two people who have agreed to provide academic references- Academic transcripts clearly listing the courses taken and grades achieved in your entire scientific higher education (bachelor’s as well as master’s or comparable degrees)
